chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sakuni al-Mazki al-Kufi in Kufa narrated that Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami said: Khalaf ibn Khalid al-Abdi narrated to us, saying: Bashr ibn Ibrahim al-Ansari narrated to us, on the authority of Thawr ibn Yazid, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma'dan, on the authority of Mu'az ibn Jabal, who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him):

I contend with you regarding Prophethood and that there is no Prophet after me, and you shall contend with the people using seven [qualities], and none from the Quraysh will argue with you regarding them, because you are the first of them in faith, the most faithful to God's pledge, the most upright in God's command, the most equitable in division, the most just in ruling the subjects, the most perceptive in judgment, and the greatest in merit before God.

key_terms.السَّوِيَّةُ: Equitable division (often referring to wealth or shares)

ai.seo_question: What are the seven characteristics that distinguish Ali ibn Abi Talib among the Quraysh according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights Ali ibn Abi Talib’s (as) unique authority to judge humanity on the Day of Resurrection based on seven specific criteria, emphasizing his status as the most faithful and just among the Quraysh. It underscores the Shia belief in Ali’s superior spiritual and judicial capacity, linking his earthly leadership to his eschatological role as the ultimate evaluator of human deeds.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-55 Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-Sakoony al-Mazaki al-Kufy in Kufa narrated that Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hazrami quoted Khalaf ibn Khalid al-Abdi, on the authority of Bashr ibn Ibrahim al-Ansari, on the authority of Soor ibn Yazid, on the authority of Khalid ibn Me’dan, on the authority of Mu’az ibn Jebal that the Prophet (MGB) told Ali (MGB), “I consider you to be in charge of my Prophethood as there shall be no more Prophets after me. You shall argue with the people using the following seven characteristics as none of the people from the Quraysh except for you possess them. The first is faith; loyalty to God’s pledge; adherence to God’s decrees; fair division of wealth; just treatment with the people; wisdom in judgements; and having the most reward near God.”
